explanation: The Royal Spanish Academy recommended the opening ¿ in 1754, so readers know from the start that a sentence is a question. Exclamations open with ¡ in the same way.

claims.text: Standard Spanish writing opens a question with an inverted question mark (¿).
Standard Portuguese, Italian and French writing does not use an opening inverted question mark.
The Royal Spanish Academy (Real Academia Española) recommended the opening question mark in 1754.
Standard Spanish opens exclamations with an inverted exclamation mark (¡).

evidence.restatement: Spanish opens every written question with an inverted question mark, as in ¿Qué hora es?
Portuguese, Italian and French mark questions only with the closing question mark.
The Real Academia Española prescribed the opening inverted question mark in its Ortografía of 1754.

Standard Spanish opens a question with an inverted question mark and closes it with the usual one.

claimResults.note: Rival test: Italian, Portuguese and French use only the closing mark. Galician and Asturian also use the opening mark but are not offered.

evidence.restatement: Portuguese, Italian and French have no opening inverted question mark.
